page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9h.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance virtualized via KVM on the x86_64 architecture. The system is powered by a dedicated 32-vCPU Hygon 7447v processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz. It is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes for persistent data.

Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing throughput without contention from noisy neighbors, though the lack of local NVMe storage requires workloads to route disk input and output over the network interface.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration avoids paying for unneeded memory capacity when running processor-bound tasks. The architecture is best suited for compute-intensive batch processing, application backends, web serving tiers, and distributed continuous integration tasks that require dedicated x86 compute threads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9h.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on KVM virtualization using the x86_64 architecture. Powered by a 32-vCPU dedicated Hygon 7447v processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, the configuration delivers consistent compute performance without virtualization thread sharing. It features 64.0 GB of system RAM, providing an exact 1:2 vCPU-to-memory balance of 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for operating system and data volumes. Networking performance provides a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps, without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its compute-focused resource ratio, the instance is suitable for compute-intensive batch operations, container worker nodes, compilation clusters, and distributed backend services.
